identity.title: Fencing and planting a garden: perimeter and area
identity.subject: MATH

pedagogy.rationale: One garden problem drives both measures: the fence (perimeter) and the planted ground (area), so learners see why they differ.

objectives.statement: Find the perimeters and areas of squares and rectangles.
objectives.subject: MATH

assumptions: Learners can measure length in metres.
Learners can add and multiply whole numbers to 100.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies the sides when asked for the perimeter, or adds them when asked for the area.
misconceptions.response: Ask what is being measured: the fence goes around (add the sides); the planting covers the inside (count or multiply the squares).

misconceptions.description: Adds only the two given side lengths for the perimeter.
misconceptions.response: Walk the shape: a rectangle has four sides, and opposite sides are equal.

scenes.title: Ma Musu's cassava garden
scenes.learnerAction: Think about the two questions Ma Musu needs to answer.

content.body:
Ma Musu in Bong County has a rectangular garden 6 metres long and 4 metres wide (illustrative numbers).

She needs to know two things: how much fence goes **around** the garden, and how much ground there is **inside** to plant cassava.

accessibility.textAlternative: A rectangular garden is 6 metres long and 4 metres wide. How much fence goes around it, and how much ground is inside?

scenes.title: What you will be able to do

content.body: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
keyPoints: Find the perimeter of a square or rectangle.
Find the area of a square or rectangle in square units.

accessibility.textAlternative: Goal: find the perimeter and the area of squares and rectangles.

scenes.title: Around or inside?
scenes.learnerAction: Open each step to see the garden drawn on squared paper.

content.body: Draw the garden on squared paper: each square is 1 metre by 1 metre. Open each step.

steps.label: Draw the garden
steps.description: A rectangle 6 squares long and 4 squares wide.

steps.label: Walk around it
steps.description: The perimeter is the distance around: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 metres of fence.

steps.label: Count the inside
steps.description: The area is the number of squares inside: 4 rows of 6 squares, 6 × 4 = 24 square metres.

media.description: A 6 by 4 rectangle on a square grid, with the border highlighted for perimeter and the squares shaded for area.
media.altText: A rectangle 6 squares long and 4 squares wide; its border measures 20 metres and it covers 24 squares.

accessibility.textAlternative: A 6 by 4 metre garden: the fence around it is 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 metres; the ground inside is 6 × 4 = 24 square metres.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Each step is a button; press Enter to open it.

offline.note: Squared exercise-book paper is the core modality.

scenes.title: A square school garden
scenes.learnerAction: Follow each step of the worked example.

content.body:
A square school garden has sides of 5 metres.

Perimeter: a square has 4 equal sides, so 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 metres, or 4 × 5 = 20 metres.

Area: 5 rows of 5 squares, 5 × 5 = 25 square metres.

The square and Ma Musu's garden have the same perimeter but different areas.

accessibility.textAlternative: A 5 metre square: perimeter 4 × 5 = 20 metres, area 5 × 5 = 25 square metres. Same perimeter as the 6 by 4 garden, different area.

scenes.title: Around or inside?
scenes.learnerAction: Choose which measure each job needs.

content.body: Each job needs either the perimeter or the area. Choose.

items.prompt: Ma Musu buys wire to go around her garden. Does she need the perimeter or the area?

options.feedback: Yes. Wire goes around the edge: that is the perimeter.
The wire goes around, not over the inside. Around is perimeter.

items.prompt: She spreads seed over all the ground inside. Does she need the perimeter or the area?

options.feedback: Seed covers the inside, not just the edge. Inside is area.
Yes. Seed covers the ground inside: that is the area.

hints: Around means perimeter; inside means area.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two jobs: buying wire to go around a garden, and spreading seed over the inside. Choose perimeter or area for each.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

scenes.title: Calculate both measures
scenes.learnerAction: Enter the perimeter and area of each garden as numbers.

content.body: Find the perimeter and the area of a garden 7 metres long and 3 metres wide, and of a square garden with 6 metre sides.

interaction.prompt: Enter the perimeter (metres) and area (square metres) for each garden.

fallback.content: Write the perimeter and the area of each garden, showing the addition or multiplication you used.

scenes.expectedObservation: 7 by 3: perimeter 20 m, area 21 square metres. 6 m square: perimeter 24 m, area 36 square metres.
hints: Draw each garden on squared paper first.

accessibility.textAlternative: Find the perimeter and area of a 7 by 3 metre garden and a 6 metre square garden.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Type each number in its labelled box.

offline.note: Work on squared paper is the core modality.

content.body: Answer each question. Your answers are checked by the school's learning system, not on this device.

fallback.content: Your teacher gives the same questions on paper and records your answers.

accessibility.textAlternative: Final questions on perimeter and area, answered with keyboard or touch.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each answer and press Space or type.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Without a device, the teacher reads each question and its choices aloud and records the spoken answer.

offline.note: Answers given on a device are scored after reconnecting; without a device the teacher gives the same questions on paper.

keyPoints: Perimeter is the distance around: add all the sides.
Area is the space inside: count the squares or multiply length by width.
Two shapes can have the same perimeter and different areas.

accessibility.textAlternative: Review: perimeter adds the sides; area counts or multiplies squares; equal perimeters can enclose different areas.
